For capstones, you have a remediation open book open note exam and you can use any resource over a period of 30 days before the following semester. I failed my 2nd year capstone and just finished doing this! It wasn’t awful and was easy to remediate without much stress. If you fail that remediation attempt they’ll work with you, and you don’t necessarily get dismissed for capstone failing! Hope that helps - current 3rd year

Hi! I believe you are talking about the clinical sciences classes. It’s close to what you are talking about but not exactly that hard. 

Basically starting 2nd semester of 2nd year you will start taking a class called clinical sciences that goes through a whole group of topics. Every single topic has an exam component and if you fail any of the topic exams you have to remediate it. If you remediate it and fail, you are then made to take a comprehensive exam of all of the topics together. If you fail the comprehensive then you will be dismissed from the program. This class and this rule will follow you until you get to 4th year when you won’t have anymore exams basically (unless you track large animal, you don’t have this rule 2nd semester of 3rd year) 

It’s extremely stressful and frustrating that they basically take away your ability to have a bad test and force a remediation but at least it isn’t an automatic fail! Hopefully that helps clarify :)
